analysis:
Examined all supplied units, including added-file modes and duplicate patch/source representations. No independently supported security regression was identified in this local scope.

scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh:28-37 runs the selected app with a cleared environment and isolated HOME, fetches metadata, and obtains runtime facts from that app. scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-models.py:60-85 selects repository identity origins, refuses redirects, bounds response sizes and retries; :109-167 matches manifests to listed artifacts and catalog IDs and verifies config.json size/SHA-256. Candidate output paths are numeric (:176-185), not remote filenames. Missing catalog artifacts are explicitly skipped (:140-144, :215-221). No weights, prompt data, tokens or release credentials are fetched by these scripts.

scripts/provider-release-publication.py adds strict cluster-runtime fields, digest syntax, unique ordered models, bounded qualification/envelope scopes, duplicate-key rejection, canonical JSON, derived-ID bounds and registration-size checks (head patch :24-185, :215-228). It loads supplied facts and includes them in release registration (:247-262, :308); schema validation does not authenticate qualification provenance or recompute runtime digests. Integration must verify the producer's binding to the final signed artifact, staging integrity, and the platform contract distinguishing release publication from independently approved qualifications (A-005, A-011, A-017, T-054, T-056, TB-011). Missing platform implementation is not evidence of a bypass.

DistributedAutomaticBatchPlannerTests.swift:931-969 tests that speculative-assistant plans do not claim public qualification; :972-1078 exercises bilateral policy persistence, compatibility and malformed-policy refusal. These tests do not establish production enforcement. Integration should reconcile the actual configuration/public-routing gates and facts producer with the new publication block and confirm that skipped models cannot acquire approvals. Encryption, cache isolation (T-041), cancellation, fan authority, billing and local add-on boundaries have no direct changes in the supplied executable scope.
